A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VLM2-Bench and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–G. Text extraction and visual inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original model evaluations, human performance, prompting experiments, annotation agreement, and case studies in Tables 1–2, Figure 5, and the appendices.

after.justification: V3 retains these original empirical results, including model and human evaluations and the prompting experiments and case studies.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction pipeline, salient sampling, paired-question construction, and CoT and visual-prompting procedures are unchanged. Appendix F retains the same prompts and detector-based cropping procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same nine subtasks across general, object-centric, and person-centric cues, totaling 3,060 queries. Figure 2 replaces an illustrative matching example without establishing a change in evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 and Figure 5 retain the same evaluated models and prompting comparisons, alongside the same human and chance baselines. The introduction's change from eight to nine open-source models is unsupported by an additional comparator in the results.

E3.justification: Equation (4) changes the counting penalty from epsilon^(-alpha) to epsilon^alpha, with the corresponding change in Appendix D.1's chance-level calculation. This revises the reported scoring rule; neither reruns nor other protocol changes are documented.

E4.justification: The cue-type error breakdown, object-versus-person comparison, prompting analyses, and Appendix G success and failure cases are retained. Figure 5's rearrangement adds no new analysis.

E5.justification: Annotation-agreement reporting and the 178/180 manual validation of GPT-4o scoring are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 have identical numerical entries, and Figure 5 reuses identical result plots. GPT-4o's reported overall score remains 60.36 and VID score 66.75. The counting-formula correction is not accompanied by revised scores or findings.

T1.justification: The exponent-sign correction changes the formal counting-accuracy definition and its chance-level expectation in Appendix D.1. For positive alpha, it removes the negative-power singularity at zero error. Other mathematical definitions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The introduction changes its claimed evaluation scope from eight to nine open-source models plus GPT-4o, contradicting the retained abstract, setup, and Table 1. The benchmark contribution, eight findings, and reported human-performance gap otherwise remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E.2 adds an explicit rationale that equal object-category sampling avoids a long-tail distribution. The Limitations section adds self-play, self-correction, and synthetic-data pretraining as possible future directions. Existing result interpretations and applicability limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The implementation disclosures, sampling instructions, detector choices, prompt templates, project-page information, and licensing statements are unchanged. The added sampling rationale and evaluator citation disclose no new implementation settings.

R1.justification: V3 adds seven references across related work, future directions, and Appendices E.2/F.1, including chart-understanding, report-generation, and training-related citations. These are limited additions; the benchmark's positioning against prior visual-understanding benchmarks remains the same.

P1.justification: V3 standardizes benchmark typography, corrects scattered grammar, adds short explanatory passages, and lightly edits related work. The section sequence, appendix organization, and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 receive visual edits, including a replacement matching example. Figure 4 replaces percentage legends with already documented counts and moves to page 5. Figure 5 moves from vertically stacked panels on page 7 to smaller horizontal panels on page 8.

improvement.justification: The correction in Equation (4) and Appendix D.1 improves the mathematical specification of counting accuracy by removing the inverse-error penalty for positive alpha. This limited benefit outweighs the new model-count inconsistency and reduced Figure 5 readability. The empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether scoring code changed.
